adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — getShortcut() is abstract with no default, and postInit calls it on every grant factory without guards (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory:74-75), so an existing custom grant extension fails with AbstractMethodError, and a null or duplicate shortcut breaks startup with NPE/IllegalStateException

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `getShortcut()` to the SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with no default implementation. In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(...)`, it iterates all `OAuth2GrantType` provider factories and unconditionally calls `gtf.getShortcut()` and then `grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName)` / `grantsToShortcuts.put(grantName, grantShortcut)`. This can (a) trigger `AbstractMethodError` at runtime for any precompiled custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation that doesn't have the new method, and (b) throw `NullPointerException` if `getShortcut()` returns null because `ConcurrentHashMap` forbids null keys/values. Duplicate shortcuts also cause startup failure via the size-mismatch `IllegalStateException` check. These are concrete, diff-grounded failure modes introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:30 — Javadoc suggests a 3-letter shortcut, but nothing checks the length: a 3-char (or ':'-containing) shortcut encodes fine and is then rejected on decode by the length()!=6 check in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider:74

adjudication.rationale: The new token-id encoding format implicitly requires a 2-character grant shortcut: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId() concatenates 2-char sessionType + 2-char tokenType + grantShort, and getTokenContextFromTokenId() enforces encodedContext.length() == 6 and slices grant shortcut as substring(4, 6). However OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() Javadoc says it is “usually like 3-letters shortcut” and there is no validation preventing 3-char (or ':'-containing) shortcuts in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(). This is a real contract/edge-case issue for custom grant implementations (could cause decode failures), but the diff’s built-in factories all return 2-char shortcuts, so it’s not an immediately verifiable broken behavior in this PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:113 — The lazy refresh in getShortcutByGrantType writes into grantsByShortcuts without the duplicate-shortcut check from postInit, so a hot-deployed grant that reuses a built-in shortcut (e.g. "ac") silently takes over decoding of existing tokens

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory#getShortcutByGrantType, the lazy-refresh path (when grantsToShortcuts lacks the grantType) does `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` and `grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut)` without checking whether `shortcut` is already mapped to a different grant. This can overwrite an existing built-in shortcut established/validated in postInit (where duplicates are only detected via size comparison), so a newly deployed grant reusing e.g. "ac" would silently replace the shortcut->grant mapping used by getGrantTypeByShortcut, changing how existing token IDs are decoded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:111 — encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException for any GRANT_TYPE value with no registered factory instead of falling back to "na", so a labelling mismatch aborts token issuance after side effects such as code consumption or session creation

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)`, the code calls `factory.getShortcutByGrantType(tokenContext.getGrantType())` and throws `IllegalStateException` if it returns null. The factory only knows shortcuts for grant types discovered via `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (plus the explicit `na` mapping). So if `ClientSessionContext` ends up with a `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` value that is not backed by a registered `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (e.g., an extension/misconfiguration, or a grant type value not present in the provider registry), access token creation will fail at `TokenManager.initToken()` when encoding the token id. However, the diff also shows a deliberate fallback to `UNKNOWN` (`na`) when the attribute is absent (`getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` sets `na` if `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` is null), and all built-in grant factories in this diff implement `getShortcut()`, so this is more an edge-case/robustness concern than a clearly verifiable defect for the changed code paths. The claim about "after side effects such as code consumption or session creation" is not directly verifiable from this diff.

Also, the decoder in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() assumes a fixed 6-char encoded context (2+2+2) and splits on `:`; postInit does not validate that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() values are exactly 2 chars and don’t contain `:`, so a custom/third-party grant could generate token IDs that later fail to decode (or decode inconsistently) with hard-to-diagnose startup/runtime errors. This is a concrete robustness/diagnosability gap introduced by the new shortcut-based encoding, but built-in shortcuts in the diff are all 2 chars so it’s not an immediate functional break in this PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — Decoder hard-codes a 6-char prefix (2-char grant shortcut) while the SPI Javadoc says shortcuts are "usually like 3-letters", so a custom grant following the Javadoc issues tokens whose IDs later fail to decode with IllegalArgumentException.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(), the decoder enforces encodedContext.length() == 6 and parses the grant shortcut as exactly 2 chars (substring(4,6)). However, encodeTokenId() simply concatenates sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShort with no length check, and OAuth2GrantTypeFactory#getShortcut() Javadoc says shortcuts are “usually like 3-letters”, i.e., not guaranteed 2. A custom grant returning a 3-char shortcut would produce token IDs whose prefix length is 7, causing the decoder to throw IllegalArgumentException (“Expected length of 6.”). This is a concrete inconsistency shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:110 — The hot-deploy refresh paths (getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut) add newly deployed grants with no duplicate-shortcut check and no null guard: a colliding shortcut silently remaps existing tokens to the wrong grant, a null shortcut NPEs on the token-issuance path, and undeployed grants are never evicted.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, the initial duplicate-shortcut validation is only performed in postInit() by comparing map sizes after bulk-loading factories. In the hot-refresh paths, getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() mutate the ConcurrentHashMaps via grantsByShortcuts.put(...) / grantsToShortcuts.put(...) without any duplicate-shortcut check, so a newly deployed grant with a colliding shortcut would overwrite an existing mapping and cause encoded token IDs to be decoded to the wrong grant. Also, getShortcutByGrantType() calls factory.getShortcut() and immediately put()s it into ConcurrentHashMap; if an implementation returns null, ConcurrentHashMap will throw NPE, impacting token issuance/encoding. The diff also shows no eviction logic for removed/undeployed grants (maps only ever grow).

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:111 — encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException (HTTP 500 on every token request) when the GRANT_TYPE attribute holds a value with no registered factory, instead of falling back to the "na" shortcut it already uses for a missing grant type.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` throws if `factory.getShortcutByGrantType(tokenContext.getGrantType())` returns null (i.e., a non-null grant type with no registered shortcut), rather than mapping it to `UNKNOWN`/"na" (even though `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext()` falls back to "na" only when the attribute is missing). However, the claim that this causes "HTTP 500 on every token request" is not supported by the diff: all modified token issuance paths set `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` to standard grant IDs that have corresponding factories/shortcuts in this PR. The issue is a robustness/edge-case concern if extensions or other code set an unregistered grant type value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:67 — getTokenContextFromTokenId throws unchecked IllegalArgumentException/NPE on malformed or null jti (including legacy/foreign IDs containing ':'), so future callers decoding untrusted tokens get 500s unless each one adds its own catch.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromTokenId, the new parsing logic does throw unchecked exceptions on bad input: it will NPE if encodedTokenId is null (calls indexOf), and it throws IllegalArgumentException for malformed formats (e.g., context part not length 6) or unknown shortcuts. The diff does not show any current call sites decoding untrusted/remote token IDs (only TokenManager encodes IDs), so the claimed 500s for future callers is an architectural/robustness concern rather than a verifiable broken behavior introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:54 — initToken now calls getShouldUseLightweightToken on every issuance, and that method dereferences session.getContext().getClient() without a null check, so any token created with no client in the session context (admin/example/programmatic issuance) NPEs.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, TokenManager.initToken() now always calls TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...), and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() calls AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session). That method (now static) dereferences session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...) with no null-check (AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java). If session.getContext().getClient() is null for any access-token issuance path, this will throw an NPE; the new call site makes this risk apply to every access token creation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1052 — session.getProvider(TokenContextEncoderProvider.class) result is used without a null check, so if the provider is unavailable or disabled every access-token issuance fails with NPE.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes TokenManager.initToken() to unconditionally do `TokenContextEncoderProvider encoder = session.getProvider(TokenContextEncoderProvider.class);` and then immediately dereference it (`encoder.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)`, `encoder.encodeTokenId(...)`) without any null check. That is a real robustness issue if the provider is not resolvable. However, this same diff also introduces and registers an internal SPI (`TokenContextEncoderSpi`) and a default factory via `META-INF/services/org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.encode.TokenContextEncoderProviderFactory`, which suggests the provider is intended to always be present in normal builds. From the diff alone we can’t verify that `getProvider(...)` can actually return null in supported runtime configurations, so the finding’s "every access-token issuance fails" claim is not fully provable as a definite defect purely from this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:102 — Context constructor now NPEs when formParams is null, captures grantType once so it goes stale after setFormParams(), and the removed public copy constructor causes NoSuchMethodError for binary custom providers that call it.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuth2GrantType.Context` constructor the new line `this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);` dereferences `formParams` (previously it was only assigned), so if any caller passes `null` this change introduces an NPE. Also, `setFormParams(...)` still only updates `this.formParams` and does not recompute `grantType`, so `getGrantType()` can become stale after `setFormParams()` is used. Finally, the public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` was removed, which is a binary-incompatible API change (would cause `NoSuchMethodError` for already-compiled code that calls it).

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — The rawTokenId null check actually re-checks grantType, so a null raw ID silently produces an "xxxxxx:null" token ID instead of failing fast.

adjudication.rationale: In `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the null check intended for `rawTokenId` is incorrectly written as `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`, so `rawTokenId` can be null without failing fast. This can propagate to `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()`, which appends `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, producing an encoded token id ending with `:null` rather than throwing (the finding’s described behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — isAccessTokenId reads the wrong offset (substring(3,5) instead of 4,6) and inverts the comparison, so it accepts wrong grant shortcuts and cannot catch encoding regressions on the token-issuance path.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the encoded context format is 6 chars (2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grantType) as implemented in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId. Therefore the grant shortcut occupies indices [4,6), but the matcher uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which is the wrong slice. Additionally, it inverts the check: `if (substring(...).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the expected shortcut and allows mismatches to pass as long as the trailing part is a UUID. This makes the test assertion ineffective and can mask regressions in the new token-id encoding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:114 — Access token jti now discloses session type (online/offline/transient), lightweight flag and grant type (e.g. password grant) to every token holder, resource server and event/tracing log

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes the access token `jti` to a structured value that encodes session type, token type (lightweight vs regular), and a 2-char grant-type shortcut (TokenManager.initToken now uses `encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx)`; DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId concatenates these fields into the ID prefix). This does indeed make that context visible anywhere the `jti` is visible (token holders/resource servers/logging of token IDs), but the code comments state this is the intended design (“encode some context into access token ID ... without ... claims”), so it’s a legitimate review concern about information disclosure/observability rather than a verifiable accidental defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:75 — getTokenContextFromTokenId throws unchecked IllegalArgumentException that echoes the raw token id, and rejects any foreign jti containing ':' (e.g. urn:uuid:...), so it becomes a latent 500 / log-injection path once it is fed untrusted token ids

adjudication.rationale: In the added `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromTokenId`, any token id containing `:` is treated as an encoded id and must have a 6-char context prefix; otherwise it throws `IllegalArgumentException` with messages that interpolate the full `encodedTokenId` (e.g., `"Incorrect token id: '" + encodedTokenId + "'. ..."`). This is a real robustness/diagnostics concern introduced by the diff (unexpected `jti` formats like `urn:uuid:...` would now throw rather than being treated as “old/unknown” as the no-colon branch does), but the diff does not show this method being invoked on untrusted/foreign token ids or logged, so the claimed latent 500/log-injection path cannot be definitively verified from the PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:113 — Lazy map refresh (encode at line 113 and decode at line 131) adds grant shortcuts without the duplicate-shortcut check done in postInit, so a later-deployed grant with a colliding shortcut silently remaps the decoded grant type

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, postInit() validates duplicate shortcuts only for the initial population of grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts. However, the lazy refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType() (adds via grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)) and getGrantTypeByShortcut() (adds via grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, newGrantType)) can overwrite an existing shortcut mapping without any duplicate/collision check. This can silently change how a 2-char shortcut decodes (getGrantTypeByShortcut uses grantsByShortcuts), potentially remapping previously-issued token IDs’ grant type after a later-deployed grant with a colliding shortcut is discovered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — The rawTokenId null check tests grantType instead, so a null raw id is accepted and produces a non-unique "xxxxxx:null" jti that would collide in jti-keyed revocation (TokenRevocationCheck)

adjudication.rationale: In the new AccessTokenContext constructor, the null-check for rawTokenId is wrong: it calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. This allows `rawTokenId` to be null, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` would then produce an encoded token id ending with `":null"` (`':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`), which is incorrect behavior and could cause collisions if such IDs were used as keys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — isAccessTokenId reads the wrong substring (3,5 instead of 4,6) and has the condition inverted (returns false on match), so "t"+grant[0] never equals any shortcut and the grant type is never checked; the matcher passes for any "xxxxxx:uuid" id (and throws StringIndexOutOfBounds instead of failing on a prefix shorter than 5 chars)

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the access token id format introduced elsewhere is 6-char context (2 session + 2 token + 2 grant) followed by ':' and a UUID. The matcher incorrectly uses items[0].substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) to extract the 2-char grant shortcut, and the condition is inverted: it returns false when the extracted substring equals expectedGrantShortcut, meaning it will accept IDs with a different grant (as long as the raw id is a UUID). It also lacks a length check on items[0], so a prefix shorter than 5 chars will throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException rather than failing the match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:82 — testIncorrectGrantType catches any RuntimeException, and it only passes because sessionFactory is null (postInit never runs), so the fallback lookup in getGrantTypeByShortcut throws an NPE; the intended IllegalArgumentException path is never checked

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before(), the factory only calls init(null) and manually populates grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts; it never calls postInit(...), so DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.sessionFactory remains null. In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut(), when the shortcut is unknown (e.g., "ac" in testIncorrectGrantType), it attempts sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...), which would NPE with a null sessionFactory before getTokenContextFromTokenId() can reach its intended IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value ... for grant type") branch. The test catches any RuntimeException and therefore would pass even if the exception is an NPE, so it does not actually validate the intended error path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:49 — The provider is built with a null session, so getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext (TRANSIENT/OFFLINE/ONLINE, lightweight vs regular, null grant falling back to "na") has no test at all, even though TokenManager.initToken uses it for every access token

adjudication.rationale: The new unit test DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest constructs DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider with a null KeycloakSession (provider = new DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider(null, factory)) and only exercises getTokenContextFromTokenId()/encodeTokenId(). It does not cover getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(), which contains nontrivial logic (deriving SessionType from userSession persistence/offline, TokenType via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), and grantType fallback to UNKNOWN when Constants.GRANT_TYPE missing). This matters because TokenManager.initToken() now calls encoder.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...) for every access token id generation, so the core path introduced by the diff lacks direct test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — No tests for malformed encoded ids: a prefix that is not 6 chars, an unknown session-type shortcut, an unknown token-type shortcut, or an encodeTokenId call with an unregistered grant type (IllegalStateException)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial parsing/validation logic in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(): it throws for encodedContext length != 6 and for unknown sessionType/tokenType/grantType shortcuts. The new DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest covers an old-token (no ':') case and an unknown grant-type shortcut case ("ofrtac:5678"), but it does not cover (a) malformed prefix length (encodedContext length != 6), (b) unknown session-type shortcut, (c) unknown token-type shortcut, or (d) encodeTokenId() failing when factory.getShortcutByGrantType() returns null for an unregistered grant type. This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage rather than a demonstrated runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:82 — The unit test fills the package-private maps directly and skips postInit, so duplicate-shortcut detection, grant discovery from real OAuth2GrantTypeFactory shortcuts, and the refresh-on-miss lookups (lines 106-137) are never exercised

adjudication.rationale: The new test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest` constructs `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory`, calls only `init(null)`, then directly assigns `factory.grantsByShortcuts` and `factory.grantsToShortcuts` (both package-visible in the diff) and never calls `postInit(KeycloakSessionFactory)`. As a result, the production logic in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(...)` (grant discovery + duplicate-shortcut validation) and the refresh-on-miss behavior in `getShortcutByGrantType` / `getGrantTypeByShortcut` (lines ~106-137) are not exercised by the unit test. This is a specific coverage/architecture issue, not a demonstrated runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:124 — Only the code/device/refresh/CIBA event helpers were switched to isAccessTokenId; expectClientLogin (client_credentials) and the password, token-exchange, UMA permission and pre-authorized code paths have no TOKEN_ID/jti assertion, so their newly wired GRANT_TYPE attributes are unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff wires GRANT_TYPE into ClientSessionContext for multiple grant flows (e.g., OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType, StandardTokenExchangeProvider, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, and refresh handling in TokenManager.validateToken) and introduces token-id encoding that depends on grant shortcuts. In AssertEvents, only a few helpers were updated to assert the new access token id format via isAccessTokenId (CODE_TO_TOKEN, DEVICE_CODE_TO_TOKEN, REFRESH_TOKEN, AUTHREQID_TO_TOKEN). The diff does not show similar TOKEN_ID assertions being added for other grant-related event helpers, so coverage of the new GRANT_TYPE wiring/encoding is plausibly incomplete. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a direct functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — Copy-paste error: the second requireNonNull checks grantType again, so a null rawTokenId gets through and is encoded as "...:null"; no constructor-validation test would catch it

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the fourth validation line is a copy/paste error: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` checks `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId`. This means `rawTokenId` can be null without being rejected, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` would then concatenate `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()` producing an encoded token id ending with `:null`. This is a real correctness defect in the introduced code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:56 — Assert.assertEquals arguments are passed as (actual, expected) throughout, so failure messages report expected and actual backwards

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest the Assert.assertEquals calls do pass the parameters in the (actual, expected) order (e.g., Assert.assertEquals(ctx.getSessionType(), AccessTokenContext.SessionType.TRANSIENT)).
